source: Transcribed from Arthur's HOW TO EARN / HOW TO SPEND TICKETS sheet and his REWARD CHART. Finley and Maryn versions are derived — see derivationNotes.

rewardChart.note: Structure is identical for all three children. Only the palette and mascot change.
rewardChart.completionMark: Same hand-drawn black check used on the weekly chore charts. Consistency across both artifacts matters — it is the same gesture to the child.
rewardChart.openQuestion: Rows of 6 with a star in the last slot, against spend tiers of 5/10/15/20, suggests each row is 5 earned tickets plus 1 milestone star. Confirm before building: is the star slot a free bonus, a savings marker, or something that goes into the Vault?

spendTiers.note: Identical for all three children. Keep it that way unless you deliberately want a per-child economy — differing prices between siblings is the fastest way to make this feel unfair.

tiers.label: 30 minutes of TV or collaborative videogame

earnCatalog.privacyRule: Any earn item flagged private:true is health-adjacent and must not appear in shared family views, exports, widgets on a shared device, or anywhere outside that child's own profile. It renders only for that child and for adults.

derivationNotes.whatWasActuallyPhotographed: Only Arthur's earn/spend sheet and only Arthur's reward chart.
howFinleyAndMarynWereBuilt: The five shared earn items are copied verbatim — they read as household-wide expectations, not Arthur-specific ones.
Spend tiers are copied verbatim and kept at family scope.
Reward chart structure (5 rows x 6, star at slot 6, vault) is copied exactly; only palette and mascot differ.
Practice Dance was pulled from Finley's and Maryn's existing weekly chore charts, where it already appears. It is the one earn item grounded in real data rather than invented.
Arthur's two therapy items were deliberately NOT copied to the other two children.
needsConfirmation: Do Finley and Maryn have their own sensory, therapy, or individual-goal items that belong on their earn lists? I did not assume they do.
Should Practice Dance actually earn a ticket, or is it already covered under 'Completing my chores' since it sits on their chore charts?
The yellow '13' handwritten in the corner of Arthur's sheet — page number in a binder, or his current ticket count?

chartPalettes.note: Row fill colors cycle down the reward chart. Row N uses cycle[(N-1) mod 3].
